evidence: The code shape the finding describes exists: ReviewUserSettingsViewSet adds no permission class of its own (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:84-96, only `scope_object = "INTERNAL"` and an unscoped queryset), so it runs the mixin's default stack — IsAuthenticated, APIScopePermission, AccessControlPermission, TeamMemberAccessPermission (posthog/api/routing.py:296-304) — all of which authorize the RAW URL team (TeamMemberAccessPermission checks `view.user_permissions.current_team.effective_membership_level`, posthog/permissions.py:214-238); `_get_or_create` then stores and reads under `resolve_effective_team_id(self.team_id)` (settings.py:98-105), which returns `team.parent_team_id or team_id` (posthog/models/scoping/manager.py:41-59), and `get_stamphog_connected` calls `has_reviewable_repo_config(instance.team_id)` on that canonical id (settings.py:71-81; products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125). The refutation is that the divergence between authorized team and stored team requires a Team with a non-null parent_team_id, and no production call path in this tree writes that column. Team.parent_team (posthog/models/team/team.py:306-312) arrives via posthog/migrations/0705_team_parent_team.py as `ADD COLUMN ... bigint NULL` plus a concurrent index, with no backfill; TeamManager.create_with_data / create (team.py:94, :176) never mention parent_team (the only `parent_team` tokens in team.py are the field at :306 and a comment at :313); TeamSerializer.create forwards validated fields plus project_id only (posthog/api/team.py:1492-1511) and `"parent_team"` appears in no serializer or admin field list (0 matches across posthog/api/team.py, posthog/api/project.py, posthog/admin/admins/team_admin.py; the admin's sole reference is the clean_* guard at team_admin.py:100-103, and it is absent from readonly_fields :137 and fieldsets :170); environment creation is hard-disabled (ProjectEnvironmentsViewSet.initial raises PermissionDenied 'Multiple environments per project are no longer available', posthog/api/team.py:2423-2429; PremiumMultiEnvironmentPermission caps one non-demo team per project, :2538-2564). A tree-wide grep for `parent_team=` / `parent_team_id=` / `parent_team = ` / `.update(parent_team` writers outside tests finds none — every non-test reference is a reader of the form `parent_team_id or team_id` (posthog/tasks/gateway_credential.py:81, posthog/models/utils.py:366-368,397-398, posthog/api/team.py:169,270, posthog/api/project.py:427,526, posthog/api/routing.py:265, posthog/storage/gateway_credential_cache.py:169,190, products/signals/backend/views.py:261,268, products/signals/backend/scout_harness/views.py:288,604, products/web_analytics/backend/api/web_analytics_achievements.py:186, products/logs/backend/presentation/views/metric_rules_api.py:72,262). The only writers are tests: products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:107 (which is the child-environment test the PR itself ships, and which only asserts the row lands on the parent), test_perspective_config_api.py:118, test_validator_config_api.py:155, test_blind_spots_config_api.py:119, products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_api.py:97,112, posthog/models/scoping/test_manager.py:129, posthog/admin/test_team_admin.py:624, posthog/storage/test/test_gateway_credential_cache.py:161,342,453. With parent_team_id always null, resolve_effective_team_id(x) == x, the authorized team and the stored team are the same row, and the described child-URL-to-parent-row path cannot be entered. The very guard the finding asks to reproduce confirms this: StamphogCanonicalTeamAccessPermission returns True immediately when `team.parent_team_id is None` (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:107-142, early return at :127), as does the logs copy (metric_rules_api.py:72), so adding it to review_hog would be a no-op in this tree. Two further points cut against the finding's framing even if the premise were reachable: (1) the shape is not new to the PR's fields — every sibling review_hog viewset canonicalizes storage under the same default URL-team permissions (products/review_hog/backend/api/perspectives.py:87,142; validators.py:95,149; blind_spots.py:97,152; reviews.py:469,625), so a fix belongs to a shared review_hog permission, not settings.py; and (2) the reachable data is narrow — the row is unique per (team, user) (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:291-292,305-308) so a caller only reads/writes their OWN parent-team preferences, `stamphog_connected` is a single existence boolean, and `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` only gates hosted Stamphog on inbox PRs where that same user is the resolved acting reviewer (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:114-140, `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` :162-200) and the team already has a synced, enabled StamphogRepoConfig for the PR's repository (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1131-1146); the toggle issues no approval itself and touches no other user's or parent-owned row.
notes: The verdict flips the moment anything populates Team.parent_team_id in production — a backfill from project_id for legacy multi-environment teams, re-enabled environment creation that sets parent_team, or admin exposure of the field — combined with a principal that has child-but-not-parent access (a private parent via access_control/RBAC, or a PAK/OAuth token scoped only to the child). Even then I would grade it `consider`, not must_fix: the exposure is one boolean (`stamphog_connected`) plus the caller's own four preference fields on the parent row, and the sibling review_hog viewsets share the shape, so the right change would be one shared canonical-team permission for review_hog rather than a settings.py-local check. I would raise to should_fix only if the endpoint were shown to reach parent-owned rows of other users or repo configs, or if a child-scoped token could flip a toggle that triggers a Stamphog approval on a repository the token's team does not own. I could not verify production data from the tree; an out-of-tree backfill would make the premise reachable.
